label: early <DEL>/f/x after a w,z,0,2,t-initial prefix (weak)
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps), and no clean description found. Activation is concentrated early in the sequence (t=1-4) and at the <DEL> step (40% of mass, with higher rates for short L). The inputs f and x are enriched (7.6x and 4.3x), and so are sequences whose first token is w, z, 0, 2 or t, which also dominate the top examples (e.g. w 2 f <DEL>, where <DEL> is the max). It never fires at t=0 and rarely fires past original position 4 or in the copy phase (11% of mass there). The best predicate (<DEL> or f/x input, t<=5, first token in {w,z,0,2,t}) gets only dev F1 0.32 and mass recall 0.43. Many activations fall outside these conditions and there are many false positives, so the unit probably reads a distributed hidden-state direction rather than a token-level property. The strongest activations are at <DEL> after short w/z/0/2/t-initial prefixes.
